text:
support-bot: ✋ FYI customer AcmeCorp reports p99 spikes on /v1/generate starting ~2026-03-17 04:10 UTC. p99 jumped from ~120ms -> ~3.2s. They included traceID trx-7f3a and sample request. Region: EU-WEST. Asking for triage.
amelia.ng: ack, adding SRE. Do we have any infra/config changes around 04:00-04:15 UTC?
mike.chang: I see a GSLB weight adjustment deployed at 04:05 (deployment id: gslb-roll-2026-03-17-04). It nudged weights for eu-west/us-east to rebalance traffic. Could cause flapping for some resolvers.
jin.ops: can you paste the customer's sample curl + timings? need connect/handshake numbers.
support-bot: sample from customer (anonymized):
```
curl -w "time_namelookup:%{time_namelookup} time_connect:%{time_connect} time_appconnect:%{time_appconnect} time_starttransfer:%{time_starttransfer}\n" -o /dev/null -s https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
# result: time_connect:0.035 time_appconnect:1.920 time_starttransfer:2.012
```
kate: appconnect (TLS handshake) jumping to ~1.9s is suspicious — not just backend slowness, likely extra RTTs or TCP setup issues.
mike.chang: running our active probe from eu-west pop -> target IP they used. probe shows TLS handshake 40ms baseline, then a sample at 04:12 with 1.7s. traceroute attached:
```
traceroute to client-ip (203.0.113.45), 30 hops max
 1  pop-eu-west 0.8 ms
 2  edge-peer-1 1.2 ms
 3  core-us-east 85.3 ms
 4  core-eu-west 86.0 ms
 5  client-net 1.2 ms
```
jin.ops: OH that's a cross-region bounce: pop -> us-east -> back to eu-west -> client. Extra transatlantic RTT explains large handshake time. Looks like some resolvers are getting us-east A record then traffic returns to eu-west.
amelia.ng: is this resolver-specific? ask customer for client resolver IP.
support-bot: customer says their resolver is 198.51.100.2 (ISP). They see TTL 20s on DNS responses.
mike.chang: dig from our eu-west pop against customer resolver shows different answers depending on EDNS: sometimes A -> 34.201.x.x (us-east), sometimes 54.89.x.x (eu-west). TTL 20 is low which makes weight changes propagate quickly.
jin.ops: root cause hypothesis: rapid GSLB weight change + low TTL + some resolvers honoring EDNS leads to route oscillation where some queries resolve to us-east IP, but network path to that IP loops back through eu-west (or client path prefers return via eu-west) causing 1 extra transatlantic RTT and TLS inflation.
kate: mitigation ideas: 1) immediately pin the customer's AS/CIDR to eu-west via a temporary override so their IP resolves to eu-west consistently; 2) roll back the GSLB weight change; 3) increase probe frequency to detect faster.
amelia.ng: support confirmed customer accepts short maintenance window for override. Can we do override ASAP?
mike.chang: filing route-override task (RO-4521). Applying IP-level route pin for 203.0.113.45/32 -> eu-west POP now.
sre-ops-bot: route override applied (RO-4521). GSLB weight rollback queued to staging.
jin.ops: probe after override shows TLS handshake back to ~42ms and p99 for AcmeCorp dropped to 0.19s. Metrics/graphs posted: p50 28ms, p95 84ms, p99 190ms.
support-bot: customer confirms they see improvement, says recovery verified from their side :thumbsup:
amelia.ng: great. Follow-ups: mike please roll back the GSLB weight change in prod (or apply a smoother ramp), jin please add a guard in the GSLB process to avoid sub-30s TTL with weight nudges, and create an alert for sudden TLS handshake inflation on per-customer basis.
mike.chang: rolling back gslb-roll-2026-03-17-04 now. I'll coordinate with release window but will push as hotfix.
jin.ops: logging notes: traceroute + dig outputs saved to cluster logs under incident trx-7f3a. Will draft brief postmortem and include proposed runbook entry: "If p99 TLS inflation + cross-region hops seen, check recent GSLB changes & resolver TTLs, apply route override." 
kate: also add a short playbook step to rate-limit weight changes over 10s windows and enforce min TTL 60s for GSLB entries when doing weight nudges.
amelia.ng: thanks team. I will update the customer with the postmortem ETA and link to the runbook once created. Closing thread once postmortem created.
support-bot: noted. closing when PM posted. :eyes:
